sections.content: If you're searching for real estate deals in Memphis TN, you've landed on one of the most investor-friendly cities in the entire country. Memphis consistently ranks among the top markets for rental yields, affordable entry prices, and high deal volume. Whether you're a first-time investor just getting started — check out our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide if you are — or a seasoned wholesaler looking to expand into new territory, Memphis deserves a serious look. This guide breaks down exactly what makes this market tick, where the best opportunities are hiding, and how to avoid the common traps that trip up out-of-state buyers.
Memphis Real Estate Market Overview

Memphis is Tennessee's largest city by population, home to roughly 630,000 residents, with a metro area exceeding 1.3 million people. The city sits on the Mississippi River and serves as a major logistics and distribution hub — FedEx is headquartered here, and Amazon, Nike, and Medline all operate massive warehouses in the area. That employment base creates steady renter demand, which is exactly what buy-and-hold investors need. As of 2024, the median home price in Memphis sits around $155,000, compared to a national median of roughly $420,000. That gap is extraordinary. You can buy a decent rental property in Memphis for what a down payment costs in markets like Denver or Austin.

Memphis also has one of the highest renter-to-owner ratios in the country. Approximately 55% of households rent rather than own. For investors, that means a massive, built-in tenant pool. Gross rental yields in Memphis commonly range from 10% to 15% on lower-priced properties, which is nearly impossible to find in coastal markets. The flip side is that Memphis does carry above-average crime rates in certain zip codes, which makes neighborhood selection critical. We'll get into that shortly.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Deals in Memphis TN

Not all of Memphis is created equal. The city has distinct pockets that perform very differently for investors. Understanding the geography before you spend a dollar is non-negotiable, especially if you're buying from out of state.
Top Investor-Friendly Neighborhoods

items: Midtown Memphis: Gentrifying area with Victorian-era homes, strong appreciation potential, and a growing young professional population. Median prices range from $180,000 to $280,000. Great for flips and mid-term rentals.

Frayser: One of the highest-yield neighborhoods in the city. Entry prices often fall between $40,000 and $80,000 with rents of $750 to $1,000 per month. High risk, high reward — tenant screening is essential here.
Whitehaven: Located in the south, near Graceland. Solid working-class neighborhood with stable rental demand. Homes typically run $70,000 to $130,000 with rents averaging $900 to $1,200.

Cordova and Germantown (East Memphis suburbs): Higher price points ($200,000 to $400,000) but lower risk, better school districts, and more stable long-term tenants. Better suited for buy-and-hold investors with more capital.
Orange Mound: One of the most active wholesale markets in the city. Very low acquisition costs, heavy investor activity, and consistent demand from Section 8 tenants.
South Memphis: Distressed properties are abundant, making it a prime hunting ground for wholesalers and flippers. Due diligence on rehab costs is critical — many homes need full gut renovations.

sections.content: Pro Tip: Before buying in any Memphis neighborhood, pull up crime maps at crimemapping.com and cross-reference with the city's blight elimination data. A $45,000 house in a war zone can destroy your returns. A $65,000 house two blocks away in a stable pocket can be a cash cow. That $20,000 difference in acquisition price is worth every penny.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Memphis
Wholesale Deals

Memphis is one of the most active wholesale markets in the South. The volume of distressed properties, motivated sellers, and active buyers makes it easy to move deals quickly. Assignment fees typically range from $5,000 to $20,000 per deal, though larger spreads are common in desirable areas. If you're new to the strategy, read our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide before diving in. Finding off-market inventory is the name of the game — driving for dollars, direct mail, and probate leads are all highly effective in Memphis. Learn more about sourcing inventory in our guide on [how to find off-market real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals).
Fix-and-Flip Opportunities

Flipping in Memphis works best in transitional neighborhoods like Midtown, Cooper-Young, and parts of North Memphis where ARVs are rising. A typical flip might involve buying at $60,000, spending $35,000 on rehab, and selling for $130,000 — leaving a gross profit of $35,000 before holding costs and financing. Always run your numbers with a reliable tool. Our free [ARV Calculator at aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) can help you quickly estimate after-repair value using local comps so you don't overpay on acquisition.
Buy-and-Hold Rental Properties

Memphis is arguably one of the best buy-and-hold markets in America for the right investor profile. The 1% rule — where monthly rent equals at least 1% of the purchase price — is still regularly achievable here. A $80,000 home renting for $900 per month clears that bar comfortably. Section 8 (Housing Choice Voucher) tenants are abundant in Memphis, and many landlords prefer the guaranteed government payments. Property management fees typically run 8% to 10% of gross rents, and many out-of-state investors choose to hire local property managers rather than self-manage across state lines.

'Memphis is where the cash flow lives. You won't find 12% gross yields in Phoenix or Nashville anymore, but Memphis still delivers if you know which zip codes to target and how to manage your properties.' — Common wisdom among mid-South real estate investors
Memphis Real Estate Market Trends in 2024

Several macro trends are shaping the Memphis market right now. First, rising interest rates have slowed retail buyer demand, which has actually helped investors in two ways: sellers are more motivated to accept lower offers, and more would-be buyers are staying in the rental market longer. Second, Memphis is seeing renewed investment in its downtown core, with new mixed-use developments and infrastructure upgrades along the riverfront. Third, institutional investors (large hedge funds and REITs) have purchased thousands of single-family homes in Memphis over the past five years, which has pushed prices up slightly in traditionally affordable zip codes like 38109 and 38127. Individual investors need to account for this competition when making offers.

Property taxes in Shelby County (which encompasses Memphis) are relatively high compared to surrounding Tennessee counties. Expect to pay roughly 1.3% to 1.5% of assessed value annually. Factor this into your cash flow projections. Insurance costs have also crept up due to nationwide pressures — budget at least $1,200 to $1,800 per year for a standard single-family rental.
Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors

Buying real estate deals in Memphis TN from out of state is completely doable — thousands of investors do it successfully every year. But it requires a different level of due diligence than buying in your backyard. Here's how to approach it intelligently.

items: Build your local team first: Find a Memphis-based real estate attorney, a property manager with strong references, a local lender or hard money lender, and a licensed contractor before you make your first offer. Your team is your eyes and ears on the ground.

Visit at least once: Make one trip to Memphis before spending serious money. Drive the neighborhoods you're targeting, visit properties in person, and meet your team face-to-face. A 2-day trip can save you from a $30,000 mistake.

Use virtual tools aggressively: Tools like Google Street View, county assessor records, and platforms like AIWholesail's [Memphis market dashboard](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/memphis-tn) give you data-driven insights without requiring boots on the ground for every deal.

Run conservative numbers: Out-of-state investors often underestimate vacancy, repairs, and management costs. Budget 10% vacancy, 10% repairs and maintenance, and 10% property management into every deal. If it still cash flows, it's a real deal.

Understand how to analyze deals before making offers: Learning to properly evaluate a deal is the single most important skill in real estate investing. Our guide on [how to analyze real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) walks you through every number you need to know.

Use a deal calculator before every offer: Gut feelings don't pay mortgages. Run every potential purchase through our free [Wholesale Deal Calculator at aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to verify your MAO (Maximum Allowable Offer) before submitting.

Network with local wholesalers: Memphis has a vibrant wholesale community. Attend local REIA meetings (Memphis Investors Group meets regularly), connect on BiggerPockets' Memphis forum, and build relationships with active wholesalers who can feed you off-market deals.

sections.content: Pro Tip: When evaluating Memphis rentals, always ask for 12 months of actual rent rolls and utility bills from the seller. Claimed rents and actual collected rents are often very different in this market. If a seller can't produce documentation, price in significant risk or walk away.
Is Memphis Right for Your Investment Strategy?

Memphis is not a market for passive, set-it-and-forget-it investors who want to buy and never think about their properties again. It requires active management, strong systems, and a solid local team. But for investors willing to do the work — or pay a quality property manager to do it for them — the returns are hard to match anywhere else at these price points. If cash flow is your priority and you're comfortable with a value-market risk profile, real estate deals in Memphis TN belong in your acquisition pipeline.
